task.description: Design a fix for ISS-0396 (Ecto.Multi {:task_records, instance_id} collision when 2+ sibling SUB_PROCESS children complete synchronously in the same transaction) per the Step-1 diagnosis, re-verifying every claim (key disambiguator uniqueness, read-your-own-writes correctness across siblings, no other reader of the old key shape, exact reachable repro path) directly against the current source rather than trusting the diagnosis's line numbers or framing.

result.summary:
Wrote lib/letflow/design/iss0396-task-records-multi-sibling-fix.md. Confirmed the collision mechanism exactly as diagnosed (TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records/6's Multi.run key at task_activation.ex:258, keyed only {:task_records, instance_id}, called once per synchronously-completing SUB_PROCESS child from build_completion_write_steps/12, sub_process.ex:966-972). CORRECTED the diagnosis's call-site framing: re-derived from resolve_parent_token_record_id/2 (engine.ex:2368-2380) and the already-merged ISS-0067 guard/test that the complete_task/3 hop-chain path (append_sub_process_children_creation_multi/6, engine.ex:2525-2545) cannot currently produce 2+ prepared_children entries at all (a same-hop-chain PARALLEL_GATEWAY split's derived branch token_ids are rejected by ISS-0067's own membership check, proven by engine_sub_process_test.exs's existing ISS-0067 test). The genuinely reachable trigger, confirmed by reading Engine.create/2's root-activation path (prepare_sub_process_children/5, engine.ex:572-605, and persist/8 -> build_sub_process_children_multi/6, engine.ex:1085-1109, which has NO such membership guard), is a definition whose graph splits into 2+ SUB_PROCESS nodes directly off a PARALLEL_GATEWAY at/near the graph root. Both call sites funnel into the same build_completion_write_steps/12, so the fix covers both regardless.

Fix design: TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records/6 gains an optional last parameter key_disambiguator (default nil, so the two existing call sites -- engine.ex:2674 maybe_append_task_activation_multi/7, and engine.ex:2009 persist_timer_fired_advance/7 -- keep compiling unchanged and keep the exact 2-tuple {:task_records, instance_id} key). Only build_completion_write_steps/12's one call site (sub_process.ex:966-972) is changed, passing parent_token.id (already in scope, already used for this same function's other 4 sibling-safe keys at sub_process.ex:960-963) as the disambiguator, producing {:task_records, instance_id, parent_token.id} for that call only.

Uniqueness re-derived: parent_token.id resolves 1:1 to parent_token_record_id (via update_parent_token_waiting/5's repo.get/repo.update round-trip, sub_process.ex:662-682), which in turn is a distinct token_id per {:sub_process_start, token_id, node_id} pending event -- distinct split branches mint distinct token ids by construction (Transition.dispatch_parallel_split/4) -- so siblings in one reduce always get pairwise-distinct parent_token.id values (TokenRecord ids are UUID PKs). Tuple-arity safety confirmed: a 2-tuple key can never == a 3-tuple key under Erlang term equality, so no collision is possible between the two unmodified call sites and the new disambiguated one, nor between a deeper cascade level's own key (maybe_cascade_to_grandparent/6 uses a distinct grandparent_token and distinct instance_id).

Correctness re-derived: load_parent_context/2 (sub_process.ex:1070-1111) issues fresh Repo reads at call time, inside the same open transaction/connection as every prior sibling's already-applied writes (Multi.merge callbacks execute in insertion order) -- Postgres read-your-own-writes visibility means sibling N's seed_state already reflects sibling N-1's inserts, so each sibling's own newly_pending diff is genuinely disjoint. Disambiguating the KEY changes only the internal Multi changes-map label for a step's result, not execution order or what a step's callback reads/writes -- purely additive, no regression risk to this property.

Other readers: grepped ':task_records' across lib/ and test/ -- confirmed exactly two production call sites of the key (the fixed-atom append_multi/6 at task_activation.ex:176, untouched, different namespace entirely; and append_multi_from_existing_records/6 at task_activation.ex:258, the one this fix touches). No downstream Multi step (reconciliation_key/event_key/projection_key/cascade_lookup_key in build_completion_write_steps/12) reads the :task_records step's own result from changes. Nothing else needs updating.

Test design specified (not implemented): a new describe block in test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs exercising Engine.create/2 directly (not complete_task/3, since that path is confirmed unreachable today per the correction above) with a new graph_root_split_into_two_subprocesses/1 fixture: START -> PARALLEL_GATEWAY(split) -> {SUB_PROCESS(sp1), SUB_PROCESS(sp2)} -> PARALLEL_GATEWAY(join) -> END, both sp1/sp2 pointing at the existing graph_child_immediate/0 (START->END, synchronous) child definition. Asserts: no raise (pre-fix would raise 'cannot merge Multi'), parent InstanceProjection reaches :completed within Engine.create/2 alone, 2 child_projections created (proves neither sibling was silently skipped -- rules out a 'first sibling wins' style non-fix), 2 SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED events, zero orphan/duplicate task rows on the root instance (this graph has no HUMAN_TASK node), and secondarily cross-checks ISS-0397's join_counters column reflects both branches joining (same shared instance_projections row, different write path, exercised incidentally not by design coupling).

Open questions flagged, not silently resolved: OQ-1, a future relaxation of ISS-0067's guard could make complete_task/3 reach this same collision -- already covered by this fix's design (same build_completion_write_steps/12 chain), no action needed now, flagged only for future traceability. OQ-2, an unbalanced/join-less split where 2 siblings might BOTH independently reach :completed and BOTH call maybe_cascade_to_grandparent/6 for the same grandparent token (a deeper, nested variant of this same collision class, one level up) -- not reachable in this design's own root-level test (no grandparent to cascade to), and possibly already foreclosed by REQ-051's own block-structured split/join validation (referenced in the existing ISS-0067 test's own comment) -- left for CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR or a follow-up issue to confirm, not assumed safe here.

No implementation code in the design doc -- verified via grep for defmodule/def/defp/'do$' patterns, none found; only prose and one @spec block.
result.routing: Route to Step 2b CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to gate lib/letflow/design/iss0396-task-records-multi-sibling-fix.md before ELIXIR-DEV/TEST-DESIGNER proceed. Pay particular attention to: (1) the §1 correction of the Step-1 diagnosis's reachable-call-site framing -- confirm independently rather than taking this design's word for it; (2) OQ-2's unresolved nested-cascade question; (3) whether the optional-parameter backward-compatibility approach (default nil, only one call site changed) is an acceptable 'in scope' backward-compatible shape per the original task brief's item 3, versus requiring an explicit follow-up issue for the two untouched call sites.
